proposed.explanation: Zoning works through inclusion and exclusion. It enables certain uses in designated zones (e.g., 'residential use is permitted here') while prohibiting the same uses elsewhere (e.g., 'residential use is prohibited in the industrial zone'). This dual mechanism guides where development happens and where it does not. Zoning allocates land use; pollution control is separate regulation (environmental law). Zoning does not control environmental impacts directly. Zoning is a neutral regulatory mechanism applicable to all properties. While zoning can have inequitable outcomes (e.g., zoning out affordable housing), that is a policy problem, not the inherent function of zoning.
